messages.subject: new home page contents
parts:
Here's a mockup of the minimal home page Andrew
requested. I'd appreciate feedback on contents
before working on formatting. Does anyone like doing
HTML formatting? If so, I'd be happy to pass off this
task, too.

mc-stan.org/index.html
====================================
STAN

Stan is a C++ package for MCMC sampling using adaptive Hamiltonian
Monte Carlo.

Download Latest
* Stan 1.0.0 (9 Aug 2012) [-> Stan download page w. license]
* RStan 1.0.0 (9 Aug 2012) [-> RStan download page w. license]

Installation and Getting Started Instructions
* Stan Command-line [->]
* RStan [->]

Manual
* Stan Modeling Language User Guide and Reference Manual [->]

Model Examples [->]

Source Code (C++ and R) [-> google code page]

Stan User Group [->]

--------------------
Copyright 2011--2012, Columbia University.
====================================

What's missing (in addition to a good once-sentence summary)
relative to the current page, ordered by importance to me:

- licensing information
- about (who built it)
- link to C++ API doc (or any info about our C++)
- e-mail contact info

- indication that we have auto-dif over
probability and linear algebra functions

- info on how to report bugs or request features
- link to developer's group, announcement group
- info on how to contribute code or models
- acknowledgments (who paid for it)
- how to cite

What I always look for first are (a) licensing info [this
is often a deal breaker], (b) manual, (c) authorship if
not indicated in manual, and (d) API doc/source code.

- Bob


On 8/10/12 5:18 PM, Andrew Gelman wrote:> Hi, Bob.
>
> 1. mc-stan.org is good for me.
>
> 2. Here's what I would put on the home page:
> a. One or two-sentence description of Stan along with the logo
> b. Status indication of latest version (e.g., "Latest versions: Stan1.03 released 9 Aug 2012, Rstan 1.1 released 10
Aug 2012")
> c. Link to instructions: How to install Stan through R
> d. Link to instructions: How to install Stan to run directly
> e. Link to Stan manual
> f. Link to page with Stan examples
> g. For more: link to googlecode page
> h. How to join the user group [with a note that info on the developer group is on the googlecode page]
>
> 3. I don't think we need most of the other things in your list below. We don't need to link to the Rstan manual,
that link can be on the "How to install Stan through R directly" page. We don't need to link to C++ API, that can be on
the googlecode page. We don't need to link to the licence info, that can be on the googlecode page. Etc.
>
> I am happy to have the google code page be as crowded as you'd like. But I'd like the homepage to be clean. Users
like me would liek the manual, the installation instructions, the examples, and to see whether anything is new. More
sophisticated people can go to the googlecode page. Thus, I'm not suggesting to remove any info, I just want to create
a clean friendly portal. Right now, I'm in the stan project but I had difficulty finding what I need.
>
> Does that make sense?
> A
>
>
> On Aug 10, 2012, at 8:26 PM, Bob Carpenter wrote:
>
>> I'm happy to create a Stan home page.
>>
>> URL:
>>
>> I like "mc-stan.org". Is everyone else OK with that?
>>
>> We'll want mc-stan.com, too, so it can forward.
>>
>> How do I create this and bill it to the project? Who
>> should the registrar be?
>>
>>
>> MAIL:
>>
>> Then we can set up mail for various features at mc-stan.org
>> and make sure they get routed to the right person. As of
>> now, we're using mc-sta...@gmail.com as the single e-mail
>> contact that forwards to me and Daniel. (We can set it up
>> to forward to a wider audience if anyone else wants in.)
>>
>>
>> HOME PAGE:
>>
>> I can layout the HTML, but the issue is what should be
>> on the page. Andrew suggests 5 or so lines that are
>> really important. That means we're going to have to
>> do some re-org and re-thinking.
>>
>> With a separate home page, the "Google Code" home page
>> function changes. Let's think top-down from the Stan
>> home page. I find the best way to do this is to consider
>> who might be visiting it and what they might want.
>>
>> At the very least, I see users coming in for the
>> latest C++/command-line or R code, wanting to know
>> where to report bugs or contact us via e-mail.
>>
>> Here's what's there now:
>>
>> * Description of what Stan is (must be suitable for all users,
>> or allow quick triage of users to their appropriate 2nd
>> tier page)
>>
>> * Status indication of latest version
>> (perhaps implicit in a link to code, etc.?)
>>
>> * Link to getting started docs
>> a. C++
>> b. command-line
>> c. RStan
>>
>> * Links to manuals
>> a. C++ API
>> b. Modeling Language + Command Line
>> c. RStan
>>
>> * Links to code downloads
>> a. latest RStan
>> b. latest C++/command-line Stan
>>
>> * Links to mailing lists
>> a. Stan Users' Group
>> b. Stan Developers' Group
>> c. Stan Announce
>> d. Stan BuildBot Status
>>
>> * License Info
>> a. Stan (BSD)
>> b. RStan (GPL)
>> c. Eigen (LGPL), Boost (Boost License)
>>
>> * Contact e-mail
>>
>> * About
>> a. who wrote it
>> b. who funded it
>>
>> * Links for Issue Tracking
>> a. reporting BUGS
>> b. suggesting features
>>
>> * Get Involved
>> a. contribute patches or more code
>> b. contribute a model
>>
>> * How to Cite Stan
>>
>> Things Andrew suggested adding:
>>
>> * Link to BUGS models
>>
>> Things people have suggested removing:
>>
>> :-)
>>
>> - Bob
>
>
